subject: Data Structure and Algorithm
chapters: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues

questions.text: Define Data Structure. Differentiate between Primitive vs Non-Primitive, and Linear vs Non-Linear data structures with examples.
Explain Abstract Data Type (ADT). Explain Time and Space Complexity analysis using Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Define Stack ADT. Explain Stack operations (PUSH, POP, PEEK) with algorithm and array implementation. Explain Overflow and Underflow conditions.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Convert the Infix expression: `(A + B) * C - (D - E) ^ (F + G)` into Postfix and Prefix expressions using Stack algorithm.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Define Circular Queue. Explain why Linear Queue suffers from false overflow. Write C functions to enqueue and dequeue elements in a Circular Queue.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Explain Priority Queue and Deque (Double Ended Queue: Input Restricted and Output Restricted Deque) with applications.
Define Linked List. Compare Static Memory Allocation (Array) vs Dynamic Memory Allocation (Linked List).
Write C functions for Singly Linked List: (a) Insert node at beginning, (b) Insert node at specified position, and (c) Delete node from end.
Explain Doubly Linked List and Circular Linked List with node structure definitions and memory diagrams.
Implement Stack and Queue data structures using Singly Linked List.
Define Binary Tree, Full Binary Tree, Complete Binary Tree, and Strictly Binary Tree. Explain Tree Traversals: Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder recursively.
Define Binary Search Tree (BST). Construct a BST by inserting keys: 45, 15, 79, 90, 10, 55, 12, 20, 50. Write algorithm to search a key in BST.
Explain AVL Tree and Balance Factor. Explain AVL rotations: LL, RR, LR, and RL rotations with numerical insertion examples.
Explain B-Tree and B+ Tree properties, structure, and applications in database indexing.
Define Graph. Differentiate between Directed vs Undirected graph, Connected vs Disconnected graph, Weighted vs Unweighted graph. Explain Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency List representations.
Explain Graph Traversal algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS) using Queue and Depth-First Search (DFS) using Stack with algorithms and step-by-step trace.
Define Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). Explain Prim's Algorithm and Kruskal's Algorithm for finding MST of a weighted graph with step-by-step numerical examples.
Explain Dijkstra's Algorithm for Single Source Shortest Path problem with algorithm and trace on a sample weighted graph.
Differentiate between Linear Search and Binary Search algorithms. Derive the Best, Average, and Worst case time complexity of Binary Search.
Explain Quick Sort algorithm using Divide and Conquer strategy. Trace Quick Sort on array: [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] using last element as pivot.
Explain Merge Sort algorithm. Derive its time complexity T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) using recurrence tree method.
Explain Heap Sort algorithm. Define Max-Heap and Min-Heap. Build a Max-Heap for keys: [12, 11, 13, 5, 6, 7] and perform heapify operation.
Define Hashing, Hash Table, and Hash Function. Explain properties of a good hash function (Division method, Multiplication method, Mid-Square method).
Explain Hash Collisions. Compare Collision Resolution Techniques: Open Addressing (Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, Double Hashing) vs Chaining (Separate Chaining).
